questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the most common reason a technically sound governance architecture design fails to get support?
options: A presentation that leads with the architecture diagram instead of the problem it solves
The architecture was designed using the wrong color scheme
ADRs are not allowed to be shown to any audience
Executives never attend any governance meetings
questions.explain: The lesson states the most common failure isn't the design itself — it's presenting it in a way that leads with architecture instead of the problem.

questions.q: Which audience, per this lesson, is described as wanting outcome, risk, and cost within the first thirty seconds?
questions.explain: Executives want outcome, risk, and cost up front, plus the specific decision needed from them — not the reference diagram first.

questions.q: What are the four parts of the presentation structure this lesson recommends?
questions.explain: The lesson's four-part structure is problem, impact, recommendation, and a specific ask — mirroring how the two case studies were told.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against using one identical presentation for every audience?
options: Only executives are allowed to see any presentation at all
The architecture stays the same, but the ordering and depth should change per audience
Each audience requires an entirely different, unrelated architecture
Operational teams should never be shown any part of the architecture
questions.explain: The content — the architecture itself — doesn't change; what changes is which parts are emphasized and in what order, per audience.

questions.q: What course does this lesson's outro say the Data Governance path continues with next?
questions.explain: The outro names Data Governance Career & Capstone as the final course in the Data Governance path.
